docs.title: Write flash
docs.text:
# Writing a new firmware to the flash memory

The following instructions were tested with Efinity 2026.1.132 on Ubuntu 24.04.5LTS.

## Prerequisites Efinix Efinity must be installed including the USB drivers for the programmer. For details see the Efintiy Software Installation User Guide.

==!!! Remove the SoM from the board to avoid damage due by misconfiguration of the IO-Voltages !!!==

## Connecting the FTDI-JTAG to the system controller

  • Set DIP-Switch SW1701.1 to "ON". This connects the JTAG-Port and COM2 to the system controller

## Setting up the Efinity Software Pogrammer - Connect the baseboard (J1701 - DEBUG) to your computer with a micro-USB-cable. - Open the programmer application USB-Target should show "(local) Kria Base-Board" - In the Programming Mode section, select SPI Active using JATG Bridge - Enable Auto configure JTAG Bridge Image - Select T20Q100F3_Jtag2Flash.bit from the release archive as the bitstream file The "FPGA"-field should show T20Q100F3 - In the Image section, select sysCntrl_flash.hex from the release archive as the bitstream file. The "FPGA"-field should show "T20Q100F3" as well. - In the SPI Active Options section, Starting Flash Address should be 0x00000000. - Enable Erase Before Programming - In the JTAG Otions section, set a JTAG Clock Speed of 7.5 MHZ or 6 MHz

docs.title: Writing the flash
docs.text: • In the Programming Mode section, klick on the Start Program button on the right After a ~15s the console should show "Programming operation completed"

docs.title: Restarting the system controller
docs.text:
• Set DIP-Switch SW1701.1 to "OFF". This disconnects the JTAG-Port and COM2 to the system controller
  • Repower the board or press the Reset-Button PB2300 to restart the system controller When board configuration has completed, the firmware toogles LED SLD0 to indicate the it has started monitoring the power supplies.

docs.title: Monitoring the power supplies
docs.text: After board start-up, the system controller reads back all power supply monitors and sends status messages over the UART (FTDI COM2) once a second. In order to reads these message, Set DIP-Switch SW1701.1 to "ON" after board start-up and open a terminal program set to 115200 Baud 8N1.

docs.title: Current Limitations
docs.text: Because of a design error, connecting the FTDI-JTAG to the system controller makes the reset button and the power-on reset ineffective (FTDI reset-out is push-pull, not open-drain). As a consequence, the FTDI-JTAG must be disconnect for a regular start-up. A patch for this problem may be inserting a diode in the reset line (not tested yet).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The build system for the Efinix Sapphire SoC firmware supports multiple build configurations with different optimization levels and debug information.

docs.title: 1. Debug Build (Default)
docs.text:
Purpose: Development and debugging

Compiler Flags: - -g3 - Maximum debug information (including macros) - -Og - Debug friendly optimization (better debuggability) - -march=rv32im_zicsr_zifencei - RISC-V ISA - -mabi=ilp32 - ABI - -DSMP - SMP support

Output Directory: app/build/debug/

Build Command:

cd app
make debug

VSCode Task: Build Debug (default build task, Ctrl+Shift+B)

Output Files: - kria_sysCntrl.elf - ELF binary with debug symbols - kria_sysCntrl.hex - Intel HEX format - kria_sysCntrl.bin - Raw binary - kria_sysCntrl.asm - Disassembly - kria_sysCntrl.map - Linker map

docs.title: 2. Release Build
docs.text:
Purpose: Production firmware

Compiler Flags: - -O3 - Maximum optimization (speed) - No debug information - -march=rv32im_zicsr_zifencei - RISC-V ISA - -mabi=ilp32 - ABI - -DSMP - SMP support

Output Directory: app/build/release/

Build Command:

cd app
make release

VSCode Task: Build Release

Output Files: - kria_sysCntrl.elf - Optimized ELF binary - kria_sysCntrl.hex - Intel HEX format - kria_sysCntrl.bin - Raw binary - kria_sysCntrl.asm - Disassembly - kria_sysCntrl.map - Linker map

docs.title: 3. Clean
docs.text:
Purpose: Remove all build artifacts

Build Command:

cd app
make clean

VSCode Task: Clean Project

Removes: - app/build/debug/ - All debug build files - app/build/release/ - All release build files - app/build/ - Build directory (if empty)

docs.title: Available Tasks
docs.text:
1. Build Debug (Default, Ctrl+Shift+B)
  2. Creates debug build

  3. Output: build/debug/

  4. Build Release

  5. Creates release build

  6. Output: build/release/

  7. Clean Project

  8. Removes all build artifacts

  9. Rebuild Debug

  10. Clean + Debug build

  11. Rebuild Release

  12. Clean + Release build

docs.title: Running Tasks
docs.text:
Via Keyboard Shortcut: - Ctrl+Shift+B - Default build task (Debug)

Via Command Palette: 1. Ctrl+Shift+P 2. Type "Tasks: Run Task" 3. Select desired task

Via Terminal Menu: - Terminal → Run Task → Select task

docs.title: Makefile Hierarchy
docs.text:
app/makefile (Project-specific)
├── mcu/software/standalone/common/bsp.mk (BSP configuration)
├── mcu/software/standalone/common/riscv64-unknown-elf.mk (Compiler flags)
└── mcu/software/standalone/common/standalone.mk (Build rules)

docs.title: Important Variables
docs.text: Variable Debug Release Description DEBUG yes no Enable debug mode DEBUG_OG no - Optimization in debug mode BENCH no yes Benchmark optimization OBJDIR build/debug build/release Output directory

docs.title: Compiler Flag Logic
docs.text:
Compiler flags are determined in riscv64-unknown-elf.mk:

# Debug configuration
ifeq ($(DEBUG),yes)
    ifneq ($(DEBUG_OG),yes)
        CFLAGS += -g3 -O0    # Maximum debug, no optimization
    else
        CFLAGS += -g3 -Og    # Debug with minimal optimization
    endif
endif

# Release configuration
ifneq ($(DEBUG),yes)
    ifneq ($(BENCH),yes)
        CFLAGS += -Os        # Size optimization
    else
        CFLAGS += -O3        # Speed optimization
    endif
endif

docs.title: Configuration Comparison
docs.text: Property Debug Release Optimization Debug (-Og) Maximum (-O3) Debug Info Full (-g3) None Code Size Larger Smaller Execution Speed Slower Faster Debuggability Good Difficult Use Case Development Production

docs.title: Toolchain
docs.text:
Compiler: riscv-none-elf-gcc

Architecture: RISC-V 32-bit - ISA: rv32im_zicsr_zifencei - ABI: ilp32 - Extensions: M (Multiply/Divide), Zicsr (CSR), Zifencei (Fence)

Linker Script: mcu/bsp/efinix/EfxSapphireSoc/linker/default.ld

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
• Use Debug builds for daily development
  • Debug builds enable better debugging with GDB/OpenOCD
  • Optimized should impact debugging much

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Test critical features with Release builds as well
  • Optimizations can reveal hidden bugs
  • Performance tests should be done with release builds

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
• Use only Release builds for production
  • Smaller code size and better performance
  • Document the build configuration used

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• For hard-to-reproduce bugs: Compare debug and release builds
  • Use -O0 instead of -Og if debug build does not show locals of interrest: bash make debug DEBUG_OG=no

docs.title: Problem: "make: command not found"
docs.text:
Solution: Ensure GNU Make is installed

sudo apt-get install build-essential

docs.title: Problem: "riscv-none-elf-gcc: command not found"
docs.text: Solution: RISC-V toolchain is not in PATH - Check toolchain installation - Set RISCV_BIN in environment or makefile

docs.title: Problem: Build artifacts not updating
docs.text:
Solution: Perform a clean build

make clean
make debug  # or make release

docs.title: Problem: Different behavior between debug and release
docs.text:
Causes: - Uninitialized variables - Race conditions - Timing-dependent code - Undefined behavior

Solution: Perform code review and static analysis

docs.title: Adding Additional Build Configuration
docs.text:
Example: Size-optimized configuration

  1. Add to app/makefile:
size:
    @echo "=== Building SIZE-OPTIMIZED configuration ==="
    @$(MAKE) -f $(firstword $(MAKEFILE_LIST)) build \
        DEBUG=no \
        BENCH=no \
        OBJDIR=build/size
  1. Add to .vscode/tasks.json:
{
  "label": "Build Size-Optimized",
  "type": "shell",
  "command": "make",
  "args": ["size"],
  "options": {
    "cwd": "${workspaceFolder}/app"
  },
  "group": "build",
  "problemMatcher": ["$gcc"],
  "detail": "Build size-optimized firmware (-Os) → build/size/"
}

docs.title: Entity: debounce
docs.text:
• File: debounce.vhd
  • Brief: Debounce / glitch filter for a single-bit input signal.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The output only follows the input after it has been stable at the new level for G_DEBOUNCE_TICKS consecutive clock cycles. Any shorter pulse resets the internal counter, so glitches are suppressed. The module can also be used as a fixed delay element for slowly changing signals (e.g. power-enable to power-good-release delays).

docs.title: Generics
docs.text: Generic name Type Value Description G_DEBOUNCE_TICKS integer 1000000 Number of consecutive stable clock cycles required before the output follows the input (1000000 ticks = 12.5 ms @ 80 MHz)

docs.title: Entity: fmcPowerCntrl
docs.text:
• File: fmcPowerCntrl.vhd
  • Brief: FMC supply power-up controller and power-good supervisor.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: FSM sequence: pwrOff -> pwrOn (rising edge of pwrCntrl_i enables the supply) -> delay (entered when the MCU releases pgood via pgoodRelease_i; waits G_PGOOD_MONITOR_DELAY ticks for the rail to rise) -> monitor (pgood_i is supervised). A low level on pwrCntrl_i in any state, or a loss of pgood_i in the monitor state, immediately returns the FSM to pwrOff and disables the supply. While the supply is off or ramping, pgood_oe is high so the open-drain pgood line is actively pulled low, preventing a false power-good indication towards the FMC module.

docs.title: Generics
docs.text: Generic name Type Value Description G_PGOOD_MONITOR_DELAY natural 8000 Number of clock ticks to wait after pgood release before pgood is monitored (accounts for rail rise time, 8000 ticks = 100 us @ 80 MHz)

docs.title: Entity: inputSync
docs.text:
• File: inputSync.vhd
  • Brief: Multi-bit input synchronizer (vector wrapper around synchronizer).

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Instantiates one single-bit synchronizer per bit of the input vector. Each bit is synchronized independently into the clk_i clock domain; there is no coherency guarantee between bits, so the module is intended for unrelated status / control inputs, not for multi-bit buses that must be sampled atomically.

docs.title: Generics
docs.text: Generic name Type Value Description WIDTH positive 1 Number of input signals to synchronize (vector width) G_INIT_VAL std_logic_vector(WIDTH - 1 downto 0) (others => '0') Per-bit initial / reset value of the synchronizer flip-flops G_NUM_GUARD_FFS natural 1 Number of guard flip-flops per bit after the capture stage (1 = classic 2-FF synchronizer)

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port name Direction Type Description clk_i in std_logic Destination clock domain, rising edge active rst_i in std_logic Asynchronous reset, high active (sets all synchronizers to G_INIT_VAL) signals_i in std_logic_vector(WIDTH - 1 downto 0) Asynchronous input vector (foreign clock domain) signals_o out std_logic_vector(WIDTH - 1 downto 0) Synchronized output vector in the clk_i domain

docs.title: Entity: synchronizer
docs.text:
• File: synchronizer.vhd
  • Brief: Single-bit clock-domain-crossing synchronizer.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Synchronizes an asynchronous input into the clk_i clock domain using a capture flip-flop followed by G_NUM_GUARD_FFS guard flip-flops (2-FF synchronizer with G_NUM_GUARD_FFS = 1). The ASYNC_REG attribute keeps the flip-flops close together and prevents X propagation on timing violations, shreg_extract disables SRL inference. Asynchronous, high-active reset initializes all stages to G_INIT_VAL.

docs.title: Generics
docs.text: Generic name Type Value Description G_INIT_VAL std_logic '0' Initial / reset value of all synchronizer flip-flops G_NUM_GUARD_FFS natural 1 Number of guard flip-flops after the capture stage (1 = classic 2-FF synchronizer, >= 2 for higher MTBF)

docs.title: Entity: sysCntrl_Top
docs.text:
• File: sysCtnrl_top.vhd
  • Brief: System controller top level for the UNV baseboard (sysCntrl).

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Instantiates the Sapphire SoC MCU and the board-level power sequencing and supervision logic. All asynchronous board inputs are synchronized (inputSync) and, where required, debounced before use. The design controls the system / PL / PS / SYZYGY / FMC power rails, overrides open-drain power-good lines while a rail is off (to avoid false power-good indications), selects the HPC / HDB VCCIO rails via break-before-make switches (vccioSelect), and generates the PS power-on-reset and Ethernet PHY reset. MCU GPIO bank 1 carries the control outputs, GPIO bank 0 reads back the synchronized status inputs.

docs.title: Entity: vccioSelect
docs.text:
• File: vccioSelect.vhd
  • Brief: Break-before-make selector between two VCCIO power rails.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Selects which of two mutually exclusive power rails is enabled (select_i = '0' -> en1_o, select_i = '1' -> en2_o). On every change of select_i both enables are deasserted for G_DELAY_TICKS clock cycles before the newly selected rail is enabled, so the two rails are never active at the same time. After reset the module starts in the delay state with both rails disabled.

docs.title: Generics
docs.text: Generic name Type Value Description G_DELAY_TICKS natural 80000 Number of clock ticks with both rails disabled during a switch-over (break-before-make delay, 80000 ticks = 1 ms @ 80 MHz)

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port name Direction Type Description clk_i in std_logic System clock, rising edge active select_i in std_logic Rail select input ('0' = enable rail 1 via en1_o, '1' = enable rail 2 via en2_o) en1_o out std_logic Enable output for VCCIO rail 1 (high = enable power, low = disable power) en2_o out std_logic Enable output for VCCIO rail 2 (high = enable power, low = disable power)

#include "boardGpio.h"

#include "bsp.h"
#include "gpio.h"
#include "boardConfig.h"

/* --- GPIO controllers ----------------------------------------------------- */
#define GPIO_IN     SYSTEM_GPIO_0_IO_CTRL
#define GPIO_OUT    SYSTEM_GPIO_1_IO_CTRL


#define GPIO_HPC_VCCIO_SELECT_MASK  (1u << GPIO_OUT_HPC_VCCIO_SELECT_BIT)
#define GPIO_HDB_VCCIO_SELECT_MASK  (1u << GPIO_OUT_HDB_VCCIO_SELECT_BIT)

#define GPIO_FMC_SUP_EN_MASK    ((1u << GPIO_OUT_FMC1_SUP_EN_BIT) | \
                                 (1u << GPIO_OUT_FMC2_SUP_EN_BIT))
#define GPIO_FMC_MOD_EN_MASK    ((1u << GPIO_OUT_FMC1_MOD_EN_BIT) | \
                                 (1u << GPIO_OUT_FMC2_MOD_EN_BIT))
#define GPIO_FMC_PG_RLS_MASK    ((1u << GPIO_OUT_FMC1_PG_RLS_BIT) | \
                                 (1u << GPIO_OUT_FMC2_PG_RLS_BIT))

#define GPIO_POR_B_MASK     (1u << GPIO_OUT_POR_B_BIT)
#define GPIO_ETH_RSTN_MASK  (1u << GPIO_OUT_ETH_RSTN_BIT)

#define GPIO_PG_MASK    (GPIO_PG_SYS_MASK | \
                    GPIO_PG_FMC1_SUP_MASK | \
                    GPIO_PG_FMC2_SUP_MASK)

static u32 gOutShadow = 0;

static void boardGpio_modifyOutput(u32 mask, u32 value)
{
    gOutShadow = (gOutShadow & ~mask) | (value & mask);
    gpio_setOutput(GPIO_OUT, gOutShadow);
}

void boardGpio_init(void)
{
    gOutShadow = 0x0;   /* supplies off, POR_B asserted, ETH PHY in reset */
    gpio_setOutput(GPIO_OUT, gOutShadow);
}

u32 boardGpio_getInput(void)
{
    return gpio_getInput(GPIO_IN);
}

void boardGpio_waitSomReady(void)
{
    u32 in = 0;

    while ((in & GPIO_SOM_READY_MASK) != GPIO_SOM_READY_MASK)
        in = gpio_getInput(GPIO_IN);
}

u32 boardGpio_getPgStatus(void)
{
    return gpio_getInput(GPIO_IN) & GPIO_PG_MASK;
}

void boardGpio_setFmcSupplyEnable(int enable)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_FMC_SUP_EN_MASK, enable ? GPIO_FMC_SUP_EN_MASK : 0u);
}

void boardGpio_setFmcPgoodRelease(int release)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_FMC_PG_RLS_MASK, release ? GPIO_FMC_PG_RLS_MASK : 0u);
}

void boardGpio_setFmcModuleEnable(int enable)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_FMC_MOD_EN_MASK, enable ? GPIO_FMC_MOD_EN_MASK : 0u);
}

void boardGpio_releaseSomPor(void)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_POR_B_MASK, GPIO_POR_B_MASK);
}

void boardGpio_releaseEthPhyReset(void)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_ETH_RSTN_MASK, GPIO_ETH_RSTN_MASK);
}

void boardGpio_pulseEthPhyReset(void)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_ETH_RSTN_MASK, 0u);
    bsp_uDelay(BOARD_ETH_RESET_PULSE_US);
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_ETH_RSTN_MASK, GPIO_ETH_RSTN_MASK);
}

void boardGpio_setHpcVccio(int sourceFmc1)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_HPC_VCCIO_SELECT_MASK, sourceFmc1 ? GPIO_HPC_VCCIO_SELECT_MASK : 0u);
}

void boardGpio_setHdbVccio(int source2V5)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_HDB_VCCIO_SELECT_MASK, source2V5 ? GPIO_HDB_VCCIO_SELECT_MASK : 0u);
}

void boardGpio_setStatusLed(int state)
{
    boardGpio_modifyOutput(GPIO_STATUS_LED_MASK, state ? GPIO_STATUS_LED_MASK : 0u);
}

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
This is the only place where GPIO bit positions are evaluated; the input/output bit positions are defined below. The output register is shadowed so that read-modify-write sequences cannot lose bits.

Note:

This file is deliberately not called gpio.h - that name is already used by the BSP driver (mcu/software/standalone/driver/gpio.h) and every src directory is on the include path.

#include "clkGen.h"

#include "bsp.h"
#include "boardConfig.h"
#include "i2cBus.h"

typedef struct {
    si5332_out_ch_t     ch;     
    u8                  enable; 
    u32                 freq_hz;    
    si5332_out_format_t format; 
} clkGenOutCfg_t;

static const clkGenOutCfg_t gOutCfg[] = {
    { SI5332_OUT_0, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT0_EN, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT0_FREQ_HZ, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT0_FORMAT },
    { SI5332_OUT_2, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT2_EN, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT2_FREQ_HZ, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT2_FORMAT },
    { SI5332_OUT_4, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT4_EN, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT4_FREQ_HZ, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT4_FORMAT },
    { SI5332_OUT_7, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT7_EN, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT7_FREQ_HZ, BOARD_CLKGEN_OUT7_FORMAT }
};

#define CLKGEN_NUM_OUT  (sizeof(gOutCfg) / sizeof(gOutCfg[0]))

static si5332_t *gClkGen = 0;

clkGen_err_t clkGen_init(void)
{
    i2cHandle_t *sysCfg = i2cBus_sysCfg();

    if (!sysCfg)
        return CLKGEN_E_INIT;

    gClkGen = si5332_initialize(I2CBUS_CLKGEN_ADDR,
                                (si5332_i2c_write_f)i2c_writeReg,
                                (si5332_i2c_read_f)i2c_readReg,
                                (void*)sysCfg);
    if (!gClkGen)
        return CLKGEN_E_INIT;

    return CLKGEN_OK;
}

clkGen_err_t clkGen_configure(void)
{
    if (!gClkGen)
        return CLKGEN_E_INIT;

    /* The clock generator sits behind the bus switch on the SysCfg bus. */
    if (i2cBus_select(I2CBUS_CH_MBRD) != I2CBUS_OK)
        return CLKGEN_E_BUS;

    /*
     * Loads the base configuration and the selected input source. Afterwards
     * only OUT6 (25 MHz) is running; OUT0/OUT2 are preconfigured but off.
     */
    if (si5332_init(gClkGen, BOARD_CLKGEN_SRC) != SI5332_OK)
        return CLKGEN_E_DEVICE;

    /*
     * Schedule format and frequency of all configurable outputs, including
     * the ones that stay off, so that clkGen_setOutputEnable() can switch
     * them on later without another commit cycle.
     */
    for (u32 i = 0; i < CLKGEN_NUM_OUT; i++) {
        if (si5332_set_output_format(gClkGen, gOutCfg[i].ch, gOutCfg[i].format) != SI5332_OK)
            return CLKGEN_E_DEVICE;

        if (si5332_set_output_freq(gClkGen, gOutCfg[i].ch, gOutCfg[i].freq_hz) != SI5332_OK) {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: Clock-Generator OUT%d frequency unsupported\r\n",
                       (int)gOutCfg[i].ch);
            return CLKGEN_E_DEVICE;
        }

        if (si5332_set_output_enable(gClkGen, gOutCfg[i].ch, gOutCfg[i].enable) != SI5332_OK)
            return CLKGEN_E_DEVICE;
    }

    /* Apply everything in one READY -> ACTIVE cycle. */
    if (si5332_commit(gClkGen) != SI5332_OK)
        return CLKGEN_E_DEVICE;

    return CLKGEN_OK;
}

clkGen_err_t clkGen_setOutputEnable(si5332_out_ch_t ch, int enable)
{
    if (!gClkGen)
        return CLKGEN_E_INIT;

    if (i2cBus_select(I2CBUS_CH_MBRD) != I2CBUS_OK)
        return CLKGEN_E_BUS;

    if (si5332_set_output_enable(gClkGen, ch, (u8)(enable ? 1 : 0)) != SI5332_OK)
        return CLKGEN_E_DEVICE;

    return CLKGEN_OK;
}

clkGen_err_t clkGen_getStatus(si5332_status_flags_t *flags)
{
    if (!flags)
        return CLKGEN_E_PARAM;
    if (!gClkGen)
        return CLKGEN_E_INIT;

    if (i2cBus_select(I2CBUS_CH_MBRD) != I2CBUS_OK)
        return CLKGEN_E_BUS;

    if (si5332_get_status(gClkGen, flags) != SI5332_OK)
        return CLKGEN_E_DEVICE;

    return CLKGEN_OK;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
// Copyright (c) 2026 Matthias Haefner - Heosys


#include "i2cBus.h"

#include "bsp.h"
#include "boardConfig.h"

/* --- Interrupt controller ------------------------------------------------- */
#define BOARD_PLIC_BASE         SYSTEM_PLIC_CTRL

/* --- I2C controller: PMBus (DC/DC converters and power monitors) ----------- */
/* --- Connected to the PMBus of the SoM ------------------------------------- */
#define I2C_PMBUS_BASE          SYSTEM_I2C_1_IO_CTRL
#define I2C_PMBUS_DEV_ID        0x1
#define I2C_PMBUS_CORE_FREQ     SYSTEM_CLINT_HZ
#define I2C_PMBUS_IF_FREQ       100000U
#define I2C_PMBUS_INTR_ID       SYSTEM_PLIC_SYSTEM_I2C_1_IO_INTERRUPT
#define I2C_PMBUS_INTR_PRIO     1U
#define I2C_PMBUS_INTR_HART     0U

/* --- I2C controller: system configuration (clock generator, add-on modules) - */
#define I2C_SYSCFG_BASE         SYSTEM_I2C_0_IO_CTRL
#define I2C_SYSCFG_DEV_ID       0x0
#define I2C_SYSCFG_CORE_FREQ    SYSTEM_CLINT_HZ
#define I2C_SYSCFG_IF_FREQ      100000U
#define I2C_SYSCFG_INTR_ID      SYSTEM_PLIC_SYSTEM_I2C_0_IO_INTERRUPT
#define I2C_SYSCFG_INTR_PRIO    2U
#define I2C_SYSCFG_INTR_HART    0U



/* Common controller timing (sampling divider and bus timeout) */
#define I2C_SAMPLING_DIVIDER    3
#define I2C_TIMEOUT_DIVIDER 10  /* timeout = coreFreq / 10 = 0.1 s */

static intrHandle_t   *gIntr     = 0;   
static i2cHandle_t    *gPmbus    = 0;   
static i2cHandle_t    *gSysCfg   = 0;   
static pi4msd5v945x_t *gBusSwitch = 0;  

static void i2cBus_buildConfig(i2cHandle_config_t *cfg, u32 base, u8 devId,
                               u8 intrId, u8 intrPrio, u8 intrHart,
                               u32 coreFreq, u32 ifFreq)
{
    cfg->baseAddress = base;
    cfg->deviceId    = devId;
    cfg->intrId      = intrId;
    cfg->intrPrio    = intrPrio;
    cfg->intrHart    = intrHart;

    cfg->cfg.samplingClockDivider = I2C_SAMPLING_DIVIDER;
    cfg->cfg.timeout = coreFreq / I2C_TIMEOUT_DIVIDER;  /* 0.1 s */
    cfg->cfg.tsuDat  = coreFreq / ifFreq / 3;           /* 3.33 us */
    cfg->cfg.tLow    = coreFreq / ifFreq / 2;           /* 5 us */
    cfg->cfg.tHigh   = coreFreq / ifFreq / 2;           /* 5 us */
    cfg->cfg.tBuf    = coreFreq / ifFreq;               /* 10 us */
}

i2cBus_err_t i2cBus_init(void)
{
    i2cHandle_config_t cfg;

    gIntr = intr_initialize(BOARD_PLIC_BASE);
    if (!gIntr)
        return I2CBUS_E_INIT;

    intr_setThreshold(gIntr, 0, 0); 

    /* I2C for power management (DC/DC converters and power monitors) */
    i2cBus_buildConfig(&cfg,
                       I2C_PMBUS_BASE, I2C_PMBUS_DEV_ID,
                       I2C_PMBUS_INTR_ID, I2C_PMBUS_INTR_PRIO,
                       I2C_PMBUS_INTR_HART,
                       I2C_PMBUS_CORE_FREQ, I2C_PMBUS_IF_FREQ); 

    gPmbus = i2c_initialize(&cfg, gIntr);
    if (!gPmbus)
        return I2CBUS_E_INIT;

    /* I2C for system configuration (clock generator, add-on modules) */
    i2cBus_buildConfig(&cfg,
                       I2C_SYSCFG_BASE, I2C_SYSCFG_DEV_ID,
                       I2C_SYSCFG_INTR_ID, I2C_SYSCFG_INTR_PRIO,
                       I2C_SYSCFG_INTR_HART,
                       I2C_SYSCFG_CORE_FREQ, I2C_SYSCFG_IF_FREQ);                  

    gSysCfg = i2c_initialize(&cfg, gIntr);
    if (!gSysCfg)
        return I2CBUS_E_INIT;

    /* Bus switch that segments the SysCfg bus */
    gBusSwitch = pi4msd5v945x_initialize(I2CBUS_BUS_SWITCH_ADDR,
                                        (pi4msd5v945x_i2c_write_f)i2c_write,
                                        (pi4msd5v945x_i2c_read_f)i2c_read,
                                        (void*)gSysCfg);
    if (!gBusSwitch)
        return I2CBUS_E_INIT;

    return I2CBUS_OK;
}

i2cBus_err_t i2cBus_select(u8 channelMask)
{
    if (!gBusSwitch)
        return I2CBUS_E_INIT;

    if (pi4msd5v945x_setChannels(gBusSwitch, channelMask) != PI4MSD5V945X_OK)
        return I2CBUS_E_SELECT;

    return I2CBUS_OK;
}

i2cHandle_t* i2cBus_pmbus(void)
{
    return gPmbus;
}

i2cHandle_t* i2cBus_sysCfg(void)
{
    return gSysCfg;
}

intrHandle_t* i2cBus_intr(void)
{
    return gIntr;
}

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Owns the interrupt controller handle, both I2C controller instances (PMBus and SysCfg) and the PI4MSD5V945X bus switch that segments the SysCfg bus. Addresses and channels are assigned here.

Note:

This file is deliberately not called i2c.h - that name is already used by the BSP driver (mcu/software/standalone/driver/i2c.h) and every src directory is on the include path.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
// Copyright (c) 2026 Matthias Haefner - Heosys


#include "interrupt.h"
#include "bsp.h"




/* The following data type defines each entry in an interrupt vector table.
 * The callback reference is the base address of the interrupting device
 * for the low level driver and an instance pointer for the high level driver.
 */
typedef struct
{
       intrHandler_t handler; 
       void *callBackRef; 
} intr_vectorTableEntry;

struct intrHandle_t
{
    u32 baseAddress;    
    u8  threshold;  
    intr_vectorTableEntry HandlerTable[PLIC_MAX_NUM_INTERRUPTS];

};

static intrHandle_t gIntrInstance;

static void intr_external(void);

void crash();
void trap_entry();



/* Public API: documented in interrupt.h only. */
intrHandle_t* intr_initialize(u32 baseAddress)
{
    intrHandle_t *pInst = &gIntrInstance;
    u8 i;

    pInst->baseAddress = baseAddress;

    for(i=0;i<PLIC_MAX_NUM_INTERRUPTS;i++)
        pInst->HandlerTable[i].handler = NULL;

    //configure RISC-V interrupt CSR
    //Set the machine trap vector (trap.S)
    csr_write(mtvec, trap_entry);
    //Enable machine external interrupts
    csr_write(mie, MIE_MEIE);
    //Enable interrupts
    csr_write(mstatus, csr_read(mstatus) | MSTATUS_MPP | MSTATUS_MIE);


    return pInst;
}

void intr_setThreshold(intrHandle_t *pInst, u8 hartId, u8 thrshld)
{
    pInst->threshold = thrshld;
    plic_set_threshold(pInst->baseAddress, hartId, pInst->threshold);
}

void intr_setEnable(intrHandle_t *pInst, u32 hartNo, u32 intrId)
{
    plic_set_enable(pInst->baseAddress, hartNo, intrId, 1);
}

void intr_setPriority(intrHandle_t *pInst, u32 intrId, u32 prio)
{
    plic_set_priority(pInst->baseAddress, intrId, prio);
}

void intr_connect(intrHandle_t *pInst, u8 intrId, intrHandler_t handler, void* pCallback)
{
    pInst->HandlerTable[intrId].handler = handler;
    pInst->HandlerTable[intrId].callBackRef = pCallback;
}

/******************************************************************************
*
* @brief This function handles exceptions and interrupts in the system.
*
* @note It is called by the trap_entry function on both exceptions and interrupts
*       events. If the cause of the trap is an interrupt, it checks the cause of
*       the interrupt and calls corresponding interrupt handler functions. If
*       the cause is an exception or an unhandled interrupt, it calls a
*       crash function to handle the error.
*
******************************************************************************/
void trap(){
    int32_t mcause = csr_read(mcause);
    int32_t interrupt = mcause < 0;
    int32_t cause     = mcause & 0xF;

    if(interrupt){
        switch(cause){
        case CAUSE_MACHINE_EXTERNAL: intr_external(); break;
        default: crash(); break;
        }
    }
    else
    {
      crash();
    }
}

/******************************************************************************
*
* @brief This function handles the system crash scenario by printing a crash message
*        and entering an infinite loop.
*
******************************************************************************/
void crash(){
    bsp_printf("\r\n*** CRASH ***\r\n");
    while(1);
}

/******************************************************************************
*
* @brief This function handles I2C interrupts by claiming pending interrupts
*        and processing them through i2c_intc().
*
******************************************************************************/
static void intr_external(){
    uint32_t claim;
    //While there is pending interrupts
    while((claim = plic_claim(gIntrInstance.baseAddress, BSP_PLIC_CPU_0)))
    {
        if(claim >= PLIC_MAX_NUM_INTERRUPTS) crash();
        if(gIntrInstance.HandlerTable[claim].handler == NULL) crash();

        gIntrInstance.HandlerTable[claim].handler(gIntrInstance.HandlerTable[claim].callBackRef);
        //unmask the claimed interrupt
        plic_release(gIntrInstance.baseAddress, BSP_PLIC_CPU_0, claim);
    }
}

#include "bsp.h"
#include "riscv.h"

#include "boardConfig.h"
#include "boardGpio.h"
#include "clkGen.h"
#include "i2cBus.h"
#include "power.h"

typedef enum {
    INIT_OK         =  0,   
    INIT_E_CLKGEN   = -1,   
    INIT_E_PWRMON   = -2,   
    INIT_E_FMCADJ   = -3    
} init_err_t;

void trap_entry();

static void cpu_enableInterrupts(void)
{
    csr_write(mtvec, trap_entry);
    csr_write(mie, MIE_MEIE);
    csr_write(mstatus, csr_read(mstatus) | MSTATUS_MPP | MSTATUS_MIE);
}

static int board_bringUp(void)
{
    int regOk = 0;

    if (i2cBus_init() != I2CBUS_OK) {
        bsp_printf("ERROR: I2C initialization failed\r\n");
        return -1;
    }

    if (pwr_init() != PWR_OK) {
        bsp_printf("ERROR: Power device initialization failed\r\n");
        return -1;
    }

    if (clkGen_init() != CLKGEN_OK) {
        bsp_printf("ERROR: Clock-Generator initialization failed\r\n");
        return -1;
    }

    cpu_enableInterrupts();

    bsp_printf("Wait for SoM supplies\r\n");
    boardGpio_waitSomReady();
    bsp_uDelay(BOARD_POWER_SETTLE_US);

    bsp_printf("Configure Clock-Generator\r\n");
    if (clkGen_configure() != CLKGEN_OK) {
        bsp_printf("ERROR: Clock-Generator configuration failed\r\n");
        return INIT_E_CLKGEN;
    }
    bsp_uDelay(BOARD_CLK_SETTLE_US);

    bsp_printf("Release ETH-PHY reset\r\n");
    boardGpio_releaseEthPhyReset();

    bsp_printf("Configure Power-Monitors\r\n");
    if (pwr_mon_configure() != PWR_OK) {
        bsp_printf("WARNING: Power-Monitor configuration incomplete\r\n");
        return INIT_E_PWRMON;
    }

    bsp_printf("Set VCCIO sources\r\n");
    boardGpio_setHpcVccio(BOARD_VCCIO_SELECT_HPC);
    boardGpio_setHdbVccio(BOARD_VCCIO_SELECT_HDB);

    bsp_printf("Enable FMC supplies\r\n");
    boardGpio_setFmcSupplyEnable(1);
    bsp_uDelay(BOARD_POWER_SETTLE_US);

    if (pwr_fmcVadj_configure() != PWR_OK) {
        bsp_printf("ERROR: FMC Vadj configuration failed\r\n");
        return INIT_E_FMCADJ;
    }

    if (pwr_fmcVadj_isRegulating(PWR_FMC1) != PWR_OK ||
        pwr_fmcVadj_isRegulating(PWR_FMC2) != PWR_OK) {
        bsp_printf("ERROR: FMC Vadj voltage register check failed\r\n");
        return INIT_E_FMCADJ;
    }

    bsp_printf("Enable FMCs\r\n");
    if (pwr_fmcVadj_enable(1) != PWR_OK) {
        bsp_printf("ERROR: FMC Vadj enable failed\r\n");
        return INIT_E_FMCADJ;
    }
    /* Release FMC power-good enable */
    boardGpio_setFmcPgoodRelease(1);

    bsp_uDelay(BOARD_POWER_SETTLE_US);

    /* Reports a supply failure as well as any monitor alert of the FMC and
     * system rails. */
    (void)pwr_checkAlerts();

    bsp_printf("Release POR\r\n");
    boardGpio_releaseSomPor();

    return INIT_OK;
}

/******************************************************************************
*
* @brief Entry point: configures the board and then supervises the supplies.
*
******************************************************************************/
void main(void)
{
    bsp_init();
    u32 LedState = 0;

    boardGpio_init();

    bsp_printf("Board configuration start\r\n");

    if (board_bringUp() != 0) {
        bsp_printf("Board configuration FAILED\r\n");
        while (1) {}
    }

    bsp_printf("Board configuration finished\r\n");

    /* Supervision loop: the power-good / ALERT lines are checked on every
     * pass (GPIO only); the measured values are reported periodically. */
    while (1) {
        if (pwr_checkAlerts() != PWR_OK)
            pwr_mon_reportFaults();

        pwr_mon_poll();
        /* Toggle LED*/
        LedState = !LedState;
        boardGpio_setStatusLed(LedState);
        bsp_uDelay(BOARD_MONITOR_PERIOD_US);
    }
}

docs.title: function pwr_checkAlerts
docs.text:
Checks the power-good / ALERT lines. 

pwr_err_t pwr_checkAlerts (
    void
)

Only if a line is low, the devices of that group are queried over I2C; faults found are merged into the sticky fault shadow. If a line is low but no device reports a fault, the supply itself failed and PWR_E_REGULATION is returned.

Returns:

PWR_OK if all lines are high, PWR_E_INIT if the monitors are not configured, PWR_E_REGULATION if a line is low, PWR_E_DEVICE if a monitor query failed.

docs.title: function pwr_mon_configure
docs.text:
Configures and arms all monitors. 

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_configure (
    void
)

ADC configuration, over-voltage, over-current and over-temperature limits, latched alert, and a clearing read of DIAG_ALRT.

Note:

Call order matters: the ALERT outputs sit on the power-good nets, so this must run after boardGpio_waitSomReady() (a latched alert would otherwise keep SYS_PG low) and before the FMC supply is switched on.

Returns:

PWR_OK if all monitors were configured, PWR_E_INIT if not initialized, PWR_E_DEVICE if at least one monitor failed (the remaining monitors are still configured).

#include "ina745a.h"
#include "tpsm8286x.h"

#include "power.h"
#include "bsp.h"
#include "userDef.h"
#include "boardGpio.h"
#include "i2cBus.h"


/* =========================================================================== */
/* Power monitors: ADC and alert behaviour (ina745a)                        */
/* =========================================================================== */
#define PWR_MON_MODE    INA745A_MODE_CONT_TEMP_CURRENT_BUSV
#define PWR_MON_VBUSCT  INA745A_CT_150US
#define PWR_MON_VSENCT  INA745A_CT_150US
#define PWR_MON_TCT     INA745A_CT_150US
#define PWR_MON_AVG     INA745A_AVG_128

/*
 * Alert configuration. Both values are dictated by the wiring (ALERT on the
 * power-good nets, see boardGpio.h):
 *   - ALATCH = 1: a fault is latched until the DIAG_ALRT register is read,
 *     so short events cannot be missed between two polls.
 *   - CNVR = 0: a conversion-ready alert would pull the power-good net low
 *     after every conversion and must stay disabled.
 *   - APOL = active low: the open-drain output pulls the net low on fault.
 */
#define PWR_MON_ALERT_LATCH 1
#define PWR_MON_ALERT_CNVR  0
#define PWR_MON_ALERT_SLOW  0   /* compare against the measured value */
#define PWR_MON_ALERT_POL   INA745A_ALERT_ACTIVE_LOW

/*
 * Under-voltage and under-current protection are not used on this board.
 * The driver API always writes both thresholds, so non-trippable values are
 * programmed: BUVL = 0 V (VBUS is unsigned, never below 0) and
 * CURRENTUL = the most negative value the 16-bit register can hold.
 */
#define PWR_MON_UV_DISABLED_V   0.0f
#define PWR_MON_UI_DISABLED_A   (-39.0f)

#define PWR_FMC_VADJ_CNTRL      (TPSM8286_FPWM_AT_VC_MASK | \
                                 TPSM8286_FPWM_MASK | \
                                 TPSM8286_OUTPUT_DISCHARGE_MASK | \
                                 TPSM8286_HICCUP_EN_MASK | \
                                 TPSM8286_VOLTAGE_RAMP_SPEED_1MV)

/* The rail table and the driver instance pool must describe the same number
 * of devices. */
typedef char pwr_assert_railCount[(PWR_RAIL_COUNT == INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES) ? 1 : -1];
typedef char pwr_assert_fmcCount[(PWR_FMC_COUNT == TPSM8286_NUM_OF_INSTANCES) ? 1 : -1];

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Static configuration                                                        */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    u8          i2cAddr;
    pwrPgLine_t pgLine;
    float       overVoltage_V;
    float       overCurrent_A;
    float       overTemp_C;
} pwrMonCfg_t;

#define X(name, addr, pg, vov, iov, tov)    { #name, addr, pg, vov, iov, tov },
static const pwrMonCfg_t gMonCfg[PWR_RAIL_COUNT] = {
    PWR_MON_TABLE
};
#undef X

typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    u8          i2cAddr;
    float       setpoint_V;
} pwrFmcCfg_t;

static const pwrFmcCfg_t gFmcCfg[PWR_FMC_COUNT] = {
    { "FMC1_VADJ", I2CBUS_FMC1_VADJ_ADDR, BOARD_FMC1_VADJ_V },
    { "FMC2_VADJ", I2CBUS_FMC2_VADJ_ADDR, BOARD_FMC2_VADJ_V }
};

static const u32 gPgMask[PWR_PG_COUNT] = {GPIO_PG_SYS_MASK,
                                    GPIO_PG_FMC1_SUP_MASK,
                                    GPIO_PG_FMC2_SUP_MASK
};

static const char * const gPgName[PWR_PG_COUNT] = {
    "SYS_PG", "FMC1_SUP_PG", "FMC2_SUP_PG"
};

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Module state                                                                 */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static tpsm8286_t *gFmcVadj[PWR_FMC_COUNT];
static ina745a_t  *gMon[PWR_RAIL_COUNT];

static pwrMon_fault_t gFaultLatch[PWR_RAIL_COUNT];

static u8 gMonConfigured;

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Helpers                                                                      */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static int pwr_mergeFaults(pwrRail_t rail, const ina745a_diag_flags_t *flags)
{
    pwrMon_fault_t *f = &gFaultLatch[rail];
    int any = 0;

    if (flags->bus_over_limit)     { f->over_voltage = 1; any = 1; }
    if (flags->current_over_limit) { f->over_current = 1; any = 1; }
    if (flags->temp_over_limit)    { f->over_temp    = 1; any = 1; }
    if (flags->power_over_limit)   { f->over_power   = 1; any = 1; }
    if (!flags->memory_ok)         { f->memory_fail  = 1; any = 1; }

    return any;
}

static int pwr_queryGroup(pwrPgLine_t line)
{
    ina745a_diag_flags_t flags;
    int faults = 0;

    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_RAIL_COUNT; i++) {
        if (gMonCfg[i].pgLine != line)
            continue;

        if (ina745a_get_diag_flags(gMon[i], &flags) != INA745A_OK)
            return -1;

        if (pwr_mergeFaults((pwrRail_t)i, &flags))
            faults++;
    }

    return faults;
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Initialization                                                               */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

pwr_err_t pwr_init(void)
{
    i2cHandle_t *pmbus = i2cBus_pmbus();

    if (!pmbus)
        return PWR_E_INIT;

    /* FMC Vadj regulators */
    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_FMC_COUNT; i++) {
        gFmcVadj[i] = tpsm8286_initialize(i, gFmcCfg[i].i2cAddr,
                                          (tpsm8286_i2c_write_f)i2c_writeReg,
                                          (tpsm8286_i2c_read_f)i2c_readReg,
                                          (void*)pmbus);
        if (!gFmcVadj[i])
            return PWR_E_INIT;
    }

    /* Power monitors; they share the PMBus with the regulators */
    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_RAIL_COUNT; i++) {
        gMon[i] = ina745a_initialize(i, gMonCfg[i].i2cAddr,
                                     (ina745a_i2c_write_f)i2c_writeRegMultipleBytes,
                                     (ina745a_i2c_read_f)i2c_readRegMultipleBytes,
                                     (void*)pmbus);
        if (!gMon[i])
            return PWR_E_INIT;
    }

    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_RAIL_COUNT; i++)
        pwr_mon_clearFaults((pwrRail_t)i);

    gMonConfigured = 0;

    return PWR_OK;
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* FMC Vadj                                                                     */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

pwr_err_t pwr_fmcVadj_configure(void)
{
    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_FMC_COUNT; i++) {
        if (!gFmcVadj[i])
            return PWR_E_INIT;

        if (gFmcCfg[i].setpoint_V > BOARD_FMC_VADJ_MAX_V) {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: %s setpoint out of range\r\n", gFmcCfg[i].name);
            return PWR_E_RANGE;
        }

        if (tpsm8286_set_cntrl(gFmcVadj[i], PWR_FMC_VADJ_CNTRL) != TPSM8286_OK)
            return PWR_E_DEVICE;

        if (tpsm8286_set_voltage(gFmcVadj[i], gFmcCfg[i].setpoint_V) != TPSM8286_OK)
            return PWR_E_DEVICE;
    }

    return PWR_OK;
}

pwr_err_t pwr_fmcVadj_isRegulating(pwrFmc_t fmc)
{
    if (fmc >= PWR_FMC_COUNT)
        return PWR_E_PARAM;
    if (!gFmcVadj[fmc])
        return PWR_E_INIT;

    int ok = 0;
    if (tpsm8286_check_voltageReg(gFmcVadj[fmc], &ok) != TPSM8286_OK)
        return PWR_E_DEVICE;

    return (ok == 1) ? PWR_OK : PWR_E_REGULATION;
}

pwr_err_t pwr_fmcVadj_enable(int enable)
{
    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_FMC_COUNT; i++) {
        if (!gFmcVadj[i])
            return PWR_E_INIT;

        if (tpsm8286_set_enable(gFmcVadj[i], enable) != TPSM8286_OK)
            return PWR_E_DEVICE;
    }

    return PWR_OK;
}

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Power monitors                                                               */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_configure(void)
{
    const ina745a_adc_config_t adcCfg = {
        .mode   = PWR_MON_MODE,
        .vbusct = PWR_MON_VBUSCT,
        .vsenct = PWR_MON_VSENCT,
        .tct    = PWR_MON_TCT,
        .avg    = PWR_MON_AVG
    };
    ina745a_alert_cfg_t alertCfg = {
        .alatch        = PWR_MON_ALERT_LATCH,
        .conv_ready_en = PWR_MON_ALERT_CNVR,
        .slow_alert    = PWR_MON_ALERT_SLOW,
        .polarity      = PWR_MON_ALERT_POL
    };
    pwr_err_t status = PWR_OK;

    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_RAIL_COUNT; i++) {
        ina745a_diag_flags_t flags;

        if (!gMon[i])
            return PWR_E_INIT;

        if (ina745a_init(gMon[i], &adcCfg) != INA745A_OK) {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: Power-Monitor %s initialization failed\r\n",
                       gMonCfg[i].name);
            status = PWR_E_DEVICE;
            continue;
        }

        /* Protection limits; the under limits are programmed to values that
         * can never trip (see PWR_MON_UV_DISABLED_V / PWR_MON_UI_DISABLED_A). */
        if (ina745a_set_bus_voltage_limits(gMon[i], gMonCfg[i].overVoltage_V,
                                           PWR_MON_UV_DISABLED_V) != INA745A_OK ||
            ina745a_set_current_limits(gMon[i], gMonCfg[i].overCurrent_A,
                                       PWR_MON_UI_DISABLED_A) != INA745A_OK ||
            ina745a_set_temperature_limit(gMon[i], gMonCfg[i].overTemp_C) != INA745A_OK) {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: Power-Monitor %s limit setup failed\r\n",
                       gMonCfg[i].name);
            status = PWR_E_DEVICE;
            continue;
        }

        /* Arm the latched alert. Writing DIAG_ALRT also clears pending
         * flags; the additional read drops anything latched in between so
         * the power-good nets start from a clean state. */
        if (ina745a_configure_alert(gMon[i], &alertCfg) != INA745A_OK) {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: Power-Monitor %s alert setup failed\r\n",
                       gMonCfg[i].name);
            status = PWR_E_DEVICE;
            continue;
        }

        (void)ina745a_get_diag_flags(gMon[i], &flags);
        pwr_mon_clearFaults((pwrRail_t)i);
    }

    gMonConfigured = 1;

    return status;
}

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_read(pwrRail_t rail, pwrMon_values_t *values)
{
    ina745a_measurements_t m;

    if (!values || rail >= PWR_RAIL_COUNT)
        return PWR_E_PARAM;
    if (!gMon[rail] || !gMonConfigured)
        return PWR_E_INIT;

    if (ina745a_get_measurements(gMon[rail], &m) != INA745A_OK)
        return PWR_E_DEVICE;

    values->bus_voltage_V = m.bus_voltage_V;
    values->current_A     = m.current_A;
    values->die_temp_C    = m.die_temp_C;

    return PWR_OK;
}

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_poll(void)
{
    pwr_err_t status = PWR_OK;

    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_RAIL_COUNT; i++) {
        pwrMon_values_t v;
        pwr_err_t res = pwr_mon_read((pwrRail_t)i, &v);

        if (res != PWR_OK) {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: Power-Monitor %s read failed\r\n", gMonCfg[i].name);
            status = res;
            continue;
        }

        bsp_printf("Pmon %7s: U=%.dmV, I=%dmA, T=%.d.%d°C\r\n",
                   gMonCfg[i].name,
                   (int)(v.bus_voltage_V * 1000.0f),
                   (int)(v.current_A * 1000.0f),
                   (int)(v.die_temp_C),(int)((v.die_temp_C - (int)(v.die_temp_C)) * 100.f));
    }
    bsp_printf("\r\n");

    return status;
}

pwr_err_t pwr_checkAlerts(void)
{
    u32 pg = boardGpio_getPgStatus();
    pwr_err_t status = PWR_OK;

    if (!gMonConfigured)
        return PWR_E_INIT;

    for (u32 line = 0; line < PWR_PG_COUNT; line++) {
        int faults;

        if (pg & gPgMask[line])
            continue;   /* line high: supply good, no alert pending */

        faults = pwr_queryGroup((pwrPgLine_t)line);

        if (faults < 0) {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: %s low, monitor query failed\r\n", gPgName[line]);
            status = PWR_E_DEVICE;
        } else {
            bsp_printf("ERROR: %s low\r\n",gPgName[line]);
            if (status == PWR_OK)
                status = PWR_E_REGULATION;      
        }
    }

    return status;
}

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_getFaults(pwrRail_t rail, pwrMon_fault_t *faults)
{
    if (!faults || rail >= PWR_RAIL_COUNT)
        return PWR_E_PARAM;

    *faults = gFaultLatch[rail];

    return PWR_OK;
}

void pwr_mon_clearFaults(pwrRail_t rail)
{
    if (rail >= PWR_RAIL_COUNT)
        return;

    gFaultLatch[rail].over_voltage = 0;
    gFaultLatch[rail].over_current = 0;
    gFaultLatch[rail].over_temp    = 0;
    gFaultLatch[rail].over_power   = 0;
    gFaultLatch[rail].memory_fail  = 0;
}

void pwr_mon_reportFaults(void)
{
    for (u32 i = 0; i < PWR_RAIL_COUNT; i++) {
        const pwrMon_fault_t *f = &gFaultLatch[i];

        if (!f->over_voltage && !f->over_current && !f->over_temp &&
            !f->over_power && !f->memory_fail)
            continue;

        bsp_printf("FAULT %s:%s%s%s%s%s\r\n", gMonCfg[i].name,
                   f->over_voltage ? " over-voltage" : "",
                   f->over_current ? " over-current" : "",
                   f->over_temp    ? " over-temperature" : "",
                   f->over_power   ? " over-power" : "",
                   f->memory_fail  ? " memory-error" : "");
    }
}

const char* pwr_railName(pwrRail_t rail)
{
    if (rail >= PWR_RAIL_COUNT)
        return "?";

    return gMonCfg[rail].name;
}

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Rails, I2C addresses, power-good groups and protection limits are defined by PWR_MON_TABLE below; the rail enum is generated from it.

Protection concept: * Over-voltage, over-current and over-temperature limits are armed with a latched alert (ALATCH = 1). Under-voltage/under-current protection is not used on this board. * The ALERT pins are wired-OR onto the power-good inputs, so a fault appears as a power-good line going low. pwr_checkAlerts() reads those lines first (no bus traffic) and only queries the devices of an affected group over I2C. * Reading DIAG_ALRT clears the latch in the device, therefore the module keeps a sticky fault shadow (see pwr_mon_getFaults()).

docs.text:
Checks the power-good / ALERT lines. 

pwr_err_t pwr_checkAlerts (
    void
)

Only if a line is low, the devices of that group are queried over I2C; faults found are merged into the sticky fault shadow. If a line is low but no device reports a fault, the supply itself failed and PWR_E_REGULATION is returned.

Returns:

docs.text:
Configures and arms all monitors. 

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_configure (
    void
)

ADC configuration, over-voltage, over-current and over-temperature limits, latched alert, and a clearing read of DIAG_ALRT.

Note:

Call order matters: the ALERT outputs sit on the power-good nets, so this must run after boardGpio_waitSomReady() (a latched alert would otherwise keep SYS_PG low) and before the FMC supply is switched on.

Returns:

PWR_OK if all monitors were configured, PWR_E_INIT if not initialized, PWR_E_DEVICE if at least one monitor failed (the remaining monitors are still configured).

docs.title: define PWR_MON_TABLE
docs.text:
Rail configuration table (X-macro). 

#define PWR_MON_TABLE `X (12V, I2CBUS_PWRMON_12V_ADDR , PWR_PG_SYS ,                            13.20f,  5.0f, 95.0f) \ X (3V3, I2CBUS_PWRMON_3V3_ADDR , PWR_PG_SYS ,                             3.60f, 12.0f, 95.0f) \ X (5V0_SOM, I2CBUS_PWRMON_5V0_ADDR , PWR_PG_SYS ,                             5.50f,  5.0f, 95.0f) \ X (1V8, I2CBUS_PWRMON_1V8_ADDR , PWR_PG_SYS ,                             1.98f,  5.0f, 95.0f) \ X (VCCADJ_FMC1, I2CBUS_PWRMON_FMC1_ADDR , PWR_PG_FMC1_SUP ,  ( BOARD_FMC_VADJ_MAX_V +0.2f),  4.5f, 95.0f) \ X (VCCADJ_FMC2, I2CBUS_PWRMON_FMC2_ADDR , PWR_PG_FMC2_SUP ,  ( BOARD_FMC_VADJ_MAX_V +0.2f),  4.5f, 95.0f)`

One row per monitored rail. This table is the only place where rails are defined; power.h/power.c derive the rail enum, the name strings, the I2C addresses, the power-good group and the protection limits from it.

Columns: * name: identifier suffix, also used as display name * addr: 7-bit I2C address on the PMBus (A0/A1 strapping) * pg: power-good / ALERT net the device is wired to (pwrPgLine_t) * vov: bus over-voltage limit [V] * iov: over-current limit [A] * tov: over-temperature limit [degC]

Note:

The number of rows must match INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES in userDef.h.

#ifndef SRC_POWER_H_
#define SRC_POWER_H_

#include <type.h>

#include "boardConfig.h"

/* =========================================================================== */
/* 5. Power monitors: per-rail configuration                                   */
/* =========================================================================== */
/*    name,        addr,                    pg,                                       vov,   iov,   tov */
#define PWR_MON_TABLE \
    X(12V,         I2CBUS_PWRMON_12V_ADDR,  PWR_PG_SYS,                            13.20f,  5.0f, 95.0f) \
    X(3V3,         I2CBUS_PWRMON_3V3_ADDR,  PWR_PG_SYS,                             3.60f, 12.0f, 95.0f) \
    X(5V0_SOM,     I2CBUS_PWRMON_5V0_ADDR,  PWR_PG_SYS,                             5.50f,  5.0f, 95.0f) \
    X(1V8,         I2CBUS_PWRMON_1V8_ADDR,  PWR_PG_SYS,                             1.98f,  5.0f, 95.0f) \
    X(VCCADJ_FMC1, I2CBUS_PWRMON_FMC1_ADDR, PWR_PG_FMC1_SUP,  (BOARD_FMC_VADJ_MAX_V+0.2f),  4.5f, 95.0f) \
    X(VCCADJ_FMC2, I2CBUS_PWRMON_FMC2_ADDR, PWR_PG_FMC2_SUP,  (BOARD_FMC_VADJ_MAX_V+0.2f),  4.5f, 95.0f)

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Status codes                                                                 */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef enum {
    PWR_OK          =  0,   
    PWR_E_PARAM     = -1,   
    PWR_E_INIT      = -2,   
    PWR_E_DEVICE    = -3,   
    PWR_E_RANGE     = -4,   
    PWR_E_REGULATION= -5    
} pwr_err_t;

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Power-good / ALERT nets                                                      */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef enum {
    PWR_PG_SYS = 0,     
    PWR_PG_FMC1_SUP,    
    PWR_PG_FMC2_SUP,    
    PWR_PG_COUNT        
} pwrPgLine_t;

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Monitored rails (generated from PWR_MON_TABLE)                               */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define X(name, addr, pg, vov, iov, tov)    PWR_RAIL_##name,
typedef enum {
    PWR_MON_TABLE
    PWR_RAIL_COUNT      
} pwrRail_t;
#undef X

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* FMC Vadj regulators                                                          */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef enum {
    PWR_FMC1 = 0,       
    PWR_FMC2,           
    PWR_FMC_COUNT       
} pwrFmc_t;

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Measurements and faults                                                      */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct {
    float bus_voltage_V;    
    float current_A;        
    float die_temp_C;       
} pwrMon_values_t;

typedef struct {
    u8 over_voltage;    
    u8 over_current;    
    u8 over_temp;       
    u8 over_power;      
    u8 memory_fail;     
} pwrMon_fault_t;

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* API                                                                          */
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

pwr_err_t pwr_init(void);


pwr_err_t pwr_fmcVadj_configure(void);

pwr_err_t pwr_fmcVadj_isRegulating(pwrFmc_t fmc);

pwr_err_t pwr_fmcVadj_enable(int enable);


pwr_err_t pwr_mon_configure(void);

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_read(pwrRail_t rail, pwrMon_values_t *values);

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_poll(void);

pwr_err_t pwr_checkAlerts(void);

pwr_err_t pwr_mon_getFaults(pwrRail_t rail, pwrMon_fault_t *faults);

void pwr_mon_clearFaults(pwrRail_t rail);

void pwr_mon_reportFaults(void);

const char* pwr_railName(pwrRail_t rail);

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Bus-agnostic core driver for the INA745A/B (40V, 16-bit, precision I2C digital power monitor with integrated 800µΩ shunt). The core only uses injected HAL callbacks (ina745a_i2c_write_f / ina745a_i2c_read_f) and never includes drivers/i2c/i2cWrapper.h or any BSP header directly. Their signature matches i2c_writeRegMultipleBytes()/i2c_readRegMultipleBytes() in drivers/i2c/i2cWrapper.h, so no adapter module is needed - callers pass them in directly via a function-pointer cast (see ina745a.h).

There is no calibration register (unlike INA226/INA228): the integrated shunt is factory-trimmed, so all LSB sizes are fixed constants (see ina745a.h and datasheet Table 8-1).

Multiple simultaneous instances are supported analogous to tpsm8286x: ina745a_initialize() takes an explicit 'devId' that directly indexes the static instance pool (size INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES, defined in userDef.h).

See also: ina745a.h

See also: plans/ina745a_driver_architecture.md

Created on: 15.11.2026

matthias

docs.title: function ina745a_initialize
docs.text:
Creates the device handle for instance devId (no I2C access).

ina745a_t * ina745a_initialize (
    u32 devId,
    u8 i2c_addr,
    ina745a_i2c_write_f w,
    ina745a_i2c_read_f r,
    void * ctx
)

Analogous to tpsm8286_initialize(): devId directly indexes the static instance pool (size INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES, defined in userDef.h), allowing multiple INA745A devices to be managed simultaneously.

Parameters:

  • devId Instance index, 0 .. (INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES - 1).
  • i2c_addr 7-bit I2C address determined by the A0/A1 pin strapping on the board (datasheet Table 6-2), validated against INA745A_ADDR_MIN .. INA745A_ADDR_MAX.
  • w HAL register write callback, must not be NULL.
  • r HAL register read callback, must not be NULL.
  • ctx Opaque context pointer passed through to w and r.

Returns:

Pointer to the device handle, or NULL if devId or i2c_addr is out of range, or w/ r is NULL.

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Register addresses (Table 7-1)                                            */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define REG_CONFIG      0x00u   
#define REG_ADC_CONFIG      0x01u   
#define REG_VBUS        0x05u   
#define REG_DIETEMP     0x06u   
#define REG_CURRENT     0x07u   
#define REG_POWER       0x08u   
#define REG_ENERGY      0x09u   
#define REG_CHARGE      0x0Au   
#define REG_DIAG_ALRT       0x0Bu   
#define REG_COL         0x0Cu   
#define REG_CUL         0x0Du   
#define REG_BOVL        0x0Eu   
#define REG_BUVL        0x0Fu   
#define REG_TEMP_LIMIT      0x10u   
#define REG_PWR_LIMIT       0x11u   
#define REG_MANUFACTURER_ID 0x3Eu   

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* CONFIG register bit positions (Table 7-3)                                 */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define CONFIG_RST_BIT      15u 
#define CONFIG_RSTACC_BIT   14u 
#define CONFIG_CONVDLY_SHIFT    6u  
#define CONFIG_CONVDLY_MASK (0xFFu << CONFIG_CONVDLY_SHIFT)

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* DIAG_ALRT register bit positions (Table 7-11)                             */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define DIAG_ALATCH_BIT     15u
#define DIAG_CNVR_BIT       14u
#define DIAG_SLOWALERT_BIT  13u
#define DIAG_APOL_BIT       12u
#define DIAG_ENERGYOF_BIT   11u
#define DIAG_CHARGEOF_BIT   10u
#define DIAG_MATHOF_BIT     9u
#define DIAG_TMPOL_BIT      7u
#define DIAG_CURRENTOL_BIT  6u
#define DIAG_CURRENTUL_BIT  5u
#define DIAG_BUSOL_BIT      4u
#define DIAG_BUSUL_BIT      3u
#define DIAG_POL_BIT        2u
#define DIAG_CNVRF_BIT      1u
#define DIAG_MEMSTAT_BIT    0u

/*
 * Number of INA745A instances that can be managed simultaneously
 * (#INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES) is defined centrally in userDef.h, analogous
 * to TPSM8286_NUM_OF_INSTANCES for tpsm8286x.
 */

#define CHK(x)  do { ina745a_err_t _e = (x); if (_e != INA745A_OK) return _e; } while (0)

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Data types                                                                 */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

struct ina745a_t {
    u8 isReady;     
    u8 isConfigured;    
    u8 i2cAddr;     
    void *hal_ctx;      
    ina745a_i2c_write_f i2c_write;  
    ina745a_i2c_read_f  i2c_read;   
};

static struct ina745a_t gInstances[INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES];

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Low-level register access                                                 */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static ina745a_err_t reg_write16(ina745a_t *d, u8 addr, u16 val)
{
    u8 buf[2] = { (u8)(val >> 8), (u8)(val & 0xFFu) };

    return d->i2c_write(d->hal_ctx, d->i2cAddr, addr, buf, sizeof(buf));
}

static ina745a_err_t reg_read16(ina745a_t *d, u8 addr, u16 *val)
{
    u8 buf[2];

    CHK(d->i2c_read(d->hal_ctx, d->i2cAddr, addr, buf, sizeof(buf)));
    *val = (u16)(((u16)buf[0] << 8) | buf[1]);
    return INA745A_OK;
}

static ina745a_err_t reg_read24(ina745a_t *d, u8 addr, u32 *val)
{
    u8 buf[3];

    CHK(d->i2c_read(d->hal_ctx, d->i2cAddr, addr, buf, sizeof(buf)));
    *val = ((u32)buf[0] << 16) | ((u32)buf[1] << 8) | buf[2];
    return INA745A_OK;
}

static ina745a_err_t reg_read40(ina745a_t *d, u8 addr, u64 *val)
{
    u8 buf[5];

    CHK(d->i2c_read(d->hal_ctx, d->i2cAddr, addr, buf, sizeof(buf)));
    *val = ((u64)buf[0] << 32) | ((u64)buf[1] << 24) | ((u64)buf[2] << 16)
         | ((u64)buf[3] << 8)  |  (u64)buf[4];
    return INA745A_OK;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Math helpers                                                              */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static s32 sign_extend32(u32 value, u8 bits)
{
    u32 m = 1u << (bits - 1);

    return (s32)((value ^ m) - m);
}

static s64 sign_extend64(u64 value, u8 bits)
{
    u64 m = 1ULL << (bits - 1);

    return (s64)((value ^ m) - m);
}

static s32 clampi(s32 x, s32 lo, s32 hi)
{
    return (x < lo) ? lo : (x > hi) ? hi : x;
}

static s32 round_f(float x)
{
    return (s32)((x >= 0.0f) ? (x + 0.5f) : (x - 0.5f));
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* ADC_CONFIG packing/unpacking (Table 7-4)                                  */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

static ina745a_err_t adc_config_pack(const ina745a_adc_config_t *cfg, u16 *raw)
{
    if (((u32)cfg->mode   & ~0xFu) || ((u32)cfg->vbusct & ~0x7u) ||
        ((u32)cfg->vsenct & ~0x7u) || ((u32)cfg->tct    & ~0x7u) ||
        ((u32)cfg->avg    & ~0x7u))
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;

    *raw = (u16)(((u16)cfg->mode   & 0xFu) << 12)
         | (u16)(((u16)cfg->vbusct & 0x7u) << 9)
         | (u16)(((u16)cfg->vsenct & 0x7u) << 6)
         | (u16)(((u16)cfg->tct    & 0x7u) << 3)
         |  (u16)((u16)cfg->avg    & 0x7u);
    return INA745A_OK;
}

static void adc_config_unpack(u16 raw, ina745a_adc_config_t *cfg)
{
    cfg->mode   = (ina745a_mode_t)((raw >> 12) & 0xFu);
    cfg->vbusct = (ina745a_convtime_t)((raw >> 9) & 0x7u);
    cfg->vsenct = (ina745a_convtime_t)((raw >> 6) & 0x7u);
    cfg->tct    = (ina745a_convtime_t)((raw >> 3) & 0x7u);
    cfg->avg    = (ina745a_avg_t)(raw & 0x7u);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* API                                                                        */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* Public API: documented in ina745a.h only. */
ina745a_t* ina745a_initialize(u32 devId, u8 i2c_addr, ina745a_i2c_write_f w, ina745a_i2c_read_f r, void *ctx)
{
    ina745a_t *pDev;

    if (!w || !r)
        return 0;
    if (i2c_addr < INA745A_ADDR_MIN || i2c_addr > INA745A_ADDR_MAX)
        return 0;
    if (devId >= INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES)
        return 0;

    pDev = &gInstances[devId];

    memset(pDev, 0, sizeof(*pDev));
    pDev->i2cAddr   = i2c_addr;
    pDev->i2c_write = w;
    pDev->i2c_read  = r;
    pDev->hal_ctx   = ctx;
    pDev->isReady   = 1;
    return pDev;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_init(ina745a_t *pDev, const ina745a_adc_config_t *cfg)
{
    u16 manuf, raw;

    if (!pDev || !cfg)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isReady)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    pDev->isConfigured = 0;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_MANUFACTURER_ID, &manuf));
    if (manuf != INA745A_MANUFACTURER_ID)
        return INA745A_E_MANUF_ID;

    CHK(adc_config_pack(cfg, &raw));
    CHK(reg_write16(pDev, REG_ADC_CONFIG, raw));

    pDev->isConfigured = 1;
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_reset(ina745a_t *pDev)
{
    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isReady)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    pDev->isConfigured = 0;
    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_CONFIG, (u16)(1u << CONFIG_RST_BIT));
}

/* Read-modify-write so that the CONVDLY field is preserved. */
ina745a_err_t ina745a_reset_accumulators(ina745a_t *pDev)
{
    u16 cfg;

    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_CONFIG, &cfg));
    cfg = (u16)((cfg & ~(1u << CONFIG_RST_BIT)) | (1u << CONFIG_RSTACC_BIT));
    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_CONFIG, cfg);
}

/* Read-modify-write: RST/RSTACC and reserved bits are left untouched. */
ina745a_err_t ina745a_set_conversion_delay(ina745a_t *pDev, u8 steps_2ms)
{
    u16 cfg;

    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_CONFIG, &cfg));
    cfg = (u16)(cfg & ~CONFIG_CONVDLY_MASK);
    cfg = (u16)(cfg | ((u16)steps_2ms << CONFIG_CONVDLY_SHIFT));
    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_CONFIG, cfg);
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_set_adc_config(ina745a_t *pDev, const ina745a_adc_config_t *cfg)
{
    u16 raw;

    if (!pDev || !cfg)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(adc_config_pack(cfg, &raw));
    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_ADC_CONFIG, raw);
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_adc_config(ina745a_t *pDev, ina745a_adc_config_t *cfg)
{
    u16 raw;

    if (!pDev || !cfg)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_ADC_CONFIG, &raw));
    adc_config_unpack(raw, cfg);
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_set_mode(ina745a_t *pDev, ina745a_mode_t mode)
{
    u16 raw;

    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_ADC_CONFIG, &raw));
    raw = (u16)((raw & (u16)~(0xFu << 12)) | (((u16)mode & 0xFu) << 12));
    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_ADC_CONFIG, raw);
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_bus_voltage(ina745a_t *pDev, float *volts)
{
    u16 raw;

    if (!pDev || !volts)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_VBUS, &raw));
    *volts = (float)raw * INA745A_BUS_VOLTAGE_LSB_V;
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_die_temperature(ina745a_t *pDev, float *celsius)
{
    u16 raw;
    s32 count;

    if (!pDev || !celsius)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_DIETEMP, &raw));
    count = sign_extend32((u32)((raw >> 4) & 0xFFFu), 12);
    *celsius = (float)count * INA745A_TEMP_LSB_C;
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_current(ina745a_t *pDev, float *amps)
{
    u16 raw;

    if (!pDev || !amps)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_CURRENT, &raw));
    *amps = (float)(s16)raw * INA745A_CURRENT_LSB_A;
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_power(ina745a_t *pDev, float *watts)
{
    u32 raw;

    if (!pDev || !watts)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read24(pDev, REG_POWER, &raw));
    *watts = (float)raw * INA745A_POWER_LSB_W;
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_energy(ina745a_t *pDev, double *joules)
{
    u64 raw;

    if (!pDev || !joules)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read40(pDev, REG_ENERGY, &raw));
    *joules = (double)raw * INA745A_ENERGY_LSB_J;
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_charge(ina745a_t *pDev, double *coulombs)
{
    u64 raw;
    s64 count;

    if (!pDev || !coulombs)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read40(pDev, REG_CHARGE, &raw));
    count = sign_extend64(raw, 40);
    *coulombs = (double)count * INA745A_CHARGE_LSB_C;
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_measurements(ina745a_t *pDev, ina745a_measurements_t *out)
{
    u16 vbus_raw, dietemp_reg, current_reg;
    u32 power_reg;
    u64 energy_reg, charge_reg;

    if (!pDev || !out)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_VBUS,    &vbus_raw));
    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_DIETEMP, &dietemp_reg));
    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_CURRENT, &current_reg));
    CHK(reg_read24(pDev, REG_POWER,   &power_reg));
    CHK(reg_read40(pDev, REG_ENERGY,  &energy_reg));
    CHK(reg_read40(pDev, REG_CHARGE,  &charge_reg));

    out->vbus_raw    = vbus_raw;
    out->dietemp_raw = (s16)sign_extend32((u32)((dietemp_reg >> 4) & 0xFFFu), 12);
    out->current_raw = (s16)current_reg;
    out->power_raw   = power_reg;
    out->energy_raw  = energy_reg;
    out->charge_raw  = sign_extend64(charge_reg, 40);

    out->bus_voltage_V = (float)out->vbus_raw    * INA745A_BUS_VOLTAGE_LSB_V;
    out->die_temp_C     = (float)out->dietemp_raw * INA745A_TEMP_LSB_C;
    out->current_A      = (float)out->current_raw * INA745A_CURRENT_LSB_A;
    out->power_W        = (float)out->power_raw   * INA745A_POWER_LSB_W;
    out->energy_J        = (double)out->energy_raw * INA745A_ENERGY_LSB_J;
    out->charge_C        = (double)out->charge_raw * INA745A_CHARGE_LSB_C;

    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_set_current_limits(ina745a_t *pDev, float over_limit_A, float under_limit_A)
{
    s32 over_c, under_c;

    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    over_c  = clampi(round_f(over_limit_A  / INA745A_CURRENT_LSB_A), -32768, 32767);
    under_c = clampi(round_f(under_limit_A / INA745A_CURRENT_LSB_A), -32768, 32767);

    CHK(reg_write16(pDev, REG_COL, (u16)(s16)over_c));
    CHK(reg_write16(pDev, REG_CUL, (u16)(s16)under_c));
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_set_bus_voltage_limits(ina745a_t *pDev, float overvoltage_V, float undervoltage_V)
{
    s32 over_c, under_c;

    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    over_c  = clampi(round_f(overvoltage_V  / INA745A_BUS_VOLTAGE_LSB_V), 0, 0x7FFF);
    under_c = clampi(round_f(undervoltage_V / INA745A_BUS_VOLTAGE_LSB_V), 0, 0x7FFF);

    CHK(reg_write16(pDev, REG_BOVL, (u16)over_c));
    CHK(reg_write16(pDev, REG_BUVL, (u16)under_c));
    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_set_temperature_limit(ina745a_t *pDev, float overtemp_C)
{
    s32 count;

    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    count = clampi(round_f(overtemp_C / INA745A_TEMP_LSB_C), -2048, 2047);
    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_TEMP_LIMIT, (u16)(((u16)((u32)count & 0xFFFu)) << 4));
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_set_power_limit(ina745a_t *pDev, float overpower_W)
{
    s32 count;

    if (!pDev)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    count = clampi(round_f(overpower_W / INA745A_PWR_LIMIT_LSB_W), 0, 0xFFFF);
    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_PWR_LIMIT, (u16)count);
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_configure_alert(ina745a_t *pDev, const ina745a_alert_cfg_t *cfg)
{
    u16 raw;

    if (!pDev || !cfg)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    raw = (u16)((cfg->alatch        ? (1u << DIAG_ALATCH_BIT)    : 0u)
              | (cfg->conv_ready_en ? (1u << DIAG_CNVR_BIT)      : 0u)
              | (cfg->slow_alert    ? (1u << DIAG_SLOWALERT_BIT) : 0u)
              | ((cfg->polarity == INA745A_ALERT_ACTIVE_HIGH) ? (1u << DIAG_APOL_BIT) : 0u));

    return reg_write16(pDev, REG_DIAG_ALRT, raw);
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_diag_flags(ina745a_t *pDev, ina745a_diag_flags_t *out)
{
    u16 raw;

    if (!pDev || !out)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isConfigured)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    CHK(reg_read16(pDev, REG_DIAG_ALRT, &raw));

    out->energy_overflow     = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_ENERGYOF_BIT)  & 1u);
    out->charge_overflow     = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_CHARGEOF_BIT)  & 1u);
    out->math_overflow       = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_MATHOF_BIT)    & 1u);
    out->temp_over_limit     = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_TMPOL_BIT)     & 1u);
    out->current_over_limit  = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_CURRENTOL_BIT) & 1u);
    out->current_under_limit = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_CURRENTUL_BIT) & 1u);
    out->bus_over_limit      = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_BUSOL_BIT)     & 1u);
    out->bus_under_limit     = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_BUSUL_BIT)     & 1u);
    out->power_over_limit    = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_POL_BIT)       & 1u);
    out->conversion_ready    = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_CNVRF_BIT)     & 1u);
    out->memory_ok           = (u8)((raw >> DIAG_MEMSTAT_BIT)   & 1u);

    return INA745A_OK;
}

ina745a_err_t ina745a_get_manufacturer_id(ina745a_t *pDev, u16 *id)
{
    if (!pDev || !id)
        return INA745A_E_PARAM;
    if (!pDev->isReady)
        return INA745A_E_NOT_INIT;

    return reg_read16(pDev, REG_MANUFACTURER_ID, id);
}

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text: Concept: * The driver core is bus-agnostic: it only uses injected HAL callbacks (ina745a_i2c_write_f / ina745a_i2c_read_f), never a concrete I2C driver directly. This allows host-side unit testing with stubs (see tests/ina745a/) without any BSP/hardware dependency, exactly like the si5332 driver. * The HAL callbacks operate on whole logical registers (1/2/3/5 bytes), MSB first, matching the INA745x register map. Their signature is intentionally identical to drivers/i2c/i2cWrapper's i2c_writeRegMultipleBytes()/i2c_readRegMultipleBytes(), so they can be passed directly to ina745a_initialize() via a function-pointer cast - no adapter module needed (same pattern as si5332 with i2c_writeReg/i2c_readReg). The core itself never includes i2cWrapper.h or any BSP header.

docs.title: function ina745a_initialize
docs.text:
Creates the device handle for instance devId (no I2C access).

ina745a_t * ina745a_initialize (
    u32 devId,
    u8 i2c_addr,
    ina745a_i2c_write_f w,
    ina745a_i2c_read_f r,
    void * ctx
)

Analogous to tpsm8286_initialize(): devId directly indexes the static instance pool (size INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES, defined in userDef.h), allowing multiple INA745A devices to be managed simultaneously.

Parameters:

  • devId Instance index, 0 .. (INA745A_NUM_INSTANCES - 1).
  • i2c_addr 7-bit I2C address determined by the A0/A1 pin strapping on the board (datasheet Table 6-2), validated against INA745A_ADDR_MIN .. INA745A_ADDR_MAX.
  • w HAL register write callback, must not be NULL.
  • r HAL register read callback, must not be NULL.
  • ctx Opaque context pointer passed through to w and r.

Returns:

Pointer to the device handle, or NULL if devId or i2c_addr is out of range, or w/ r is NULL.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
// Copyright (c) 2026 Matthias Haefner - Heosys



#include "pi4msd5v945x.h"

struct pi4msd5v945x_t {
    int isReady;    
    u8 i2cAddr; 
    void* hal_ctx;  
    pi4msd5v945x_i2c_write_f i2c_write; 
    pi4msd5v945x_i2c_read_f i2c_read;   
};



static pi4msd5v945x_t gDevice;

/* Public API: documented in pi4msd5v945x.h only. */
pi4msd5v945x_t* pi4msd5v945x_initialize(u8 i2c_addr, pi4msd5v945x_i2c_write_f w, pi4msd5v945x_i2c_read_f r, void *ctx )
{
    pi4msd5v945x_t* pDev = &gDevice;

    pDev->i2cAddr = i2c_addr;
    pDev->i2c_write = w;
    pDev->i2c_read = r;
    pDev->hal_ctx = ctx;
    pDev->isReady = 1;

    return pDev;
}


pi4msd5v945x_err_t pi4msd5v945x_setChannels(pi4msd5v945x_t *pDev, u8 channels)
{
    if (!pDev) return PI4MSD5V945X_E_PARAM;

    pDev->i2c_write(pDev->hal_ctx, pDev->i2cAddr,&channels,1);

    return PI4MSD5V945X_OK;
}

docs.title: function id_encode
docs.text:
Encodes a fractional divider N = num/den into the 15-bit register triple. 

static void id_encode (
    u32 num,
    u32 den,
    u16 * intg,
    u16 * res,
    u16 * den_reg
)

Formula verified against the ID_TEST reference export (no -512 offset, as stated in the Si5332 reference manual): 

INTG = floor(128 * num / den)
RES  = (128 * num) mod den
DEN  = den

Parameters:

  • num Divider numerator.
  • den Divider denominator.
  • intg INTG register value.
  • res RES register value.
  • den_reg DEN register value (equals den).

docs.title: function plan_id
docs.text:
Plans a fresh (currently unused) MultiSynth divider for frequency f .

static si5332_err_t plan_id (
    u32 f,
    u32 * num,
    u32 * den,
    u8 * r
)

Selects the smallest R divider for which the resulting N = VCO_HZ / (f*R) fits into the 15-bit fractional divider (# ID_N_MIN <= N < 256), then approximates N with rational_approx() using a denominator up to ID_DEN_MAX.

Parameters:

  • f Desired output frequency in Hz.
  • num Numerator of the resulting divider N = num/den.
  • den Denominator of the resulting divider N = num/den.
  • r Resulting R divider (1..63).

Returns:

SI5332_OK on success, SI5332_E_FREQ_UNSUPPORTED if no valid (R, N) combination exists for f.

docs.title: function rational_approx
docs.text:
Computes the best rational approximation of n/d with a bounded denominator. 

static void rational_approx (
    u64 n,
    u64 d,
    u32 max_den,
    u32 * out_n,
    u32 * out_d
)

Uses a continued-fraction expansion with semiconvergents. If n/d is exactly representable with a denominator <= max_den, the reduced fraction is returned.

Parameters:

  • n Numerator of the target ratio.
  • d Denominator of the target ratio.
  • max_den Maximum allowed denominator of the result.
  • out_n Numerator of the approximation.
  • out_d Denominator of the approximation (1 <= out_d <= max_den).

docs.text:
Writes (or powers down) one output channel from the shadow state. 

static si5332_err_t write_channel (
    si5332_t * d,
    int i
)

Always writes OUTx_MODE. If the channel is configured, writes the complete register set (OUTx_DIV, OMUX byte, power-down bits) because the CBPro export omits registers of blocks that were unused at export time. If the channel is not configured, only the OMUX and OUTx power-down bits are set to disable the block.
